newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila T-bills up on higher reserve requirements.
newsitem.headline: Manila T-bills up on higher reserve requirements.

text.p: Manila banks quoted higher bid and offer rates in the secondary market on Wednesday after the central bank imposed additional reserve requirements on banks, traders said.
"Everyone wants to be long on pesos in case liquidity tightens. There would be 11 billion pesos out of the system," a trader said.
The central bank raised on Tuesday the liquidity reserve requirement to three percent from two percent.
The central bank's action was intended to curtail liquidity that might have been used for peso speculation.
A trader said there were rumours in the market the central bank may further raise the reserve requirement.
"Nobody wants to move in the secondary market. And banks are having a hard time selling the cash management bills," he said.
Traders said banks would only start positioning on T-bills when the market normalises. The peso had been under pressure for months due to the spillover effects of the Thai baht's problems.
The average interbank call loan rate was unchanged at 22.03125 percent, with 20 lenders and 13 borrowers.
Volume was lower at 11.28 billion pesos from 12.41 billion.
